about: Persistent photo-to-model findings. Open findings are comparison work, not permission to move geometry. Never delete history or close from a software pass. See docs/CONTINUOUS_LOOP.md.

discrepancies.description: Compare the current water/construction/deck edges separately, including the squared deck tongue east of the steps. The approved loop PRD records this difference; measure the current model before correcting it.
discrepancies.resolution: 15 Nov: both deck tongues corrected as a measured change (data/pool_ring_corrections.json): changed edges 0.14 m rms on 39 picks and 0.18 m rms on 9 held-out picks through IMG_2204-2206, reviewed and approved with notes by a second agent (data/placement_reviews.json measuredApprovals measured-north-pool-ring-tongues; docs/reviews/pool-deck-outline/REVIEW.md).

discrepancies.description: Inventory and compare the white pool-side box, parasols, plants and trees against the current Inspect Details render. Record individual missing or misplaced items before building; split this finding by feature as needed.
Resolve the northwest terrace/stair position and visible floor limits. Existing records flag uncertain concealed ends and a possible eastward offset; do not treat these as a measured correction.
Keep concealed patio ground edges and Isabel-side access widths unresolved until ground corners can be identified independently. This does not block visible pool, deck or facade corrections.

Registry part3's notch corner (-179.4, 33.7) projects about 40 px (0.4-0.5 m at 12 m) east of the near block's edge in IMG_2206 through the solved station camera, and the block's top reads about 1 m higher in the photo than the two-storey model. One camera only: not a measured correction until a second solved camera or the lidar confirms it.

IMG_2206 and IMG_2208 show white patio walls about 1.8 m high with curved cappings and brown plank doors south of the west path; the model has 1 m generated garden walls there, in the right place but without height, cappings or doors. Door feet are hidden by planting.

The south-west deck tongue's north edge has a recess about 0.5-0.6 m wide where the ladder stands (IMG_2205 x 48-100, IMG_2206 x 1475-1510); the corrected ring runs straight across it. Two held-out picks in the ring measurement were interpolated across it (without them held-out is 0.17 m rms, n=7).

The pool ladders render as small arcs barely above the coping; IMG_2204 and IMG_2205 show tall goose-neck stainless rails anchored on the deck. Positions now match the photos; the fitting's size or height (pool_ladder in src/slice.ts and src/pool-kit.ts) does not.

The pump box (o4) is now placed and turned as photographed, but the model draws louvres on all four sides where IMG_2204 and IMG_2205 show them on the front-right face only, and it is 1.1 m long against about 1.2 m. The shower post beside it is not modelled.

Near the north row's house fronts the roof station cannot fix depth: furniture, door feet and awning attachments cast 1-3 m from the registry fronts (some behind them), and the two station cameras differ by 0.6-1.6 m in depth at the patio front. The laser survey's roof fit moves the resort's footprints about 1.5 m north, but barely improves. The re-traced north patios, path and lawn edge use IMG_2205; furniture and awnings are placed relative to the registry fronts. A second camera station (ground level, from the lawn) would allow a measured correction of the patio front and test the registry fronts.

IMG_2199 shows the patio pergola's beam on the garden wall starting at the closed door's raised coping, which puts the beam end at or just south of the aerial-inferred dividing wall; the pergola is drawn against the north side of that wall. Which patio the pergola belongs to, and whether the divider meets the garden wall where inferred, needs a view from inside the patios.

On the north side of Calle Jorge the Esri and Google aerials show a white patio wall square to the lane at about 111.1 m, from the house corner of 6364401UF1366S_part2 to the planters, and the first brick entrance about 2 m west of it. The model's planter entrances (data/jorge_lane.json boundary gaps 112.4-113.5 and 114.7-115.8 m, with their number niches) were placed from photo pins (±2-5 m), and the garden end placed the same way proved 4 m too far east. Built as they are, a wall at 111.1 m would stand between the first entrance and the patio IMG_2230 shows it leading into, so that wall is left out (independent review, docs/reviews/lane-walls/). Needs the planter entrances re-placed against the aerial or a square-on photo (photo request jorge-east-square-on); walls at 117.5 and 124.5 m should be re-checked against them then.

The laser survey (PNOA-LiDAR 2020-21, 1 m ground model, sampled every 0.5 m along the Cervantes centreline) has the lane level at +0.53 m from 47.5 m along it eastwards and at +1.13-1.17 m from 42.5 m westwards: the 0.6 m drop is centred about 45 m along the lane. The photo-placed flight and ramp (data/cervantes_elena_steps.json, cervantes-elena-ramp) run from the drain at 49.1 m to 46.1 m, centred about 47.6 m, so the survey puts the drop about 2 m further west; the model is up to about 0.4 m above the survey at 46-47 m (independent review of 17 November 2026). A 1 m ground model widens a 3 m ramp, and the camera pins near the junction are 1.5-4.7 m, so this alone does not justify moving the reviewed flight, garden door, beds and lawns that hang off the drain. Settle it before detail goes on the junction with a solved camera: IMG_2286 has the drain, the tile grid and the door (scripts/photo_pose.py), with IMG_2464 or IMG_2328 as the second view. 17 November 2026 (Dave: the ramp and steps in front of the Elena 24 door are not in the right place; task elena-junction-lawns-roof): moved. IMG_2262 shows the foot drain meeting the near lawn's north-east kerb corner; that corner lies on the lane kerb measured through two solved roof cameras, and the lawn's north kerb from it to the measured west-wall corner is about 10-11 tile rows in IMG_2262, as the model's 4.6 m, so the drain belongs at the corner: 2.0 m west of where it was (the new drain line passes 0.04 m from the corner). The 2020-21 survey (1 m) has the rise starting 2.0-2.5 m west of the old foot (the 2014-15 2 m survey about 0.7 m; plan registration is about 1 m). IMG_2196 has the drain 1.4-1.75 m west of the garden door's centre (0.72 m before), and the two solved roof cameras put the door 0.6-0.9 m west of its old place. Flight, ramp (and the matching Cervantes lane vertices, a straight run), terrain ramp and level items moved 2.0 m; the garden door, its steps, patio and east planter 1.0 m; the hedge bed between them stretched (its west end 0.25 m short of the flight top so it stays above the ground); the Cervantes north garden wall's east end follows the door wall. Not a measured placement: no ground camera at the junction is solved yet. See docs/reviews/cervantes-elena-steps-position. Second-agent review (REVIEW.md): approved as an estimated correction; still open, the lawn north-kerb length (10-10.5 tile rows against 4.6 m) and the door's width.

The lane-edge 'patio walls' of data/cervantes_patio_walls.json are 0.65 m high on both sides from the Dalí exit to east of Elena. In the November photos (IMG_2264, IMG_2467, IMG_2468, IMG_2274) the bed edges on the north side are low rounded kerbs of about 0.15-0.2 m with the planting standing over them, and on the south side the houses and garden walls come down to the lane. 17 November 2026: cervantes-patio-north-1 lowered to 0.15 m with the new at-grade bed behind it (independent review); the other four (south-1, south-2, south-3, north-east) are still 0.65 m. 17 November 2026 (Dave): south-2 split at the Elena lawns' west wall; the stretch along the near Elena lawn is now the 0.15 m kerb IMG_2262, IMG_2286 and IMG_2328 show, carried to the lawn corner at the foot drain; the stretch west of the wall (cervantes-patio-south-2-west) stays 0.65 m. src/cervantes-walls.ts drew every one of these walls 0.21 m above its recorded height (it stood them on the stored 0.27 m road height instead of the lane surface at 0.06 m); fixed, so north-1 now shows its 0.15 m and the 0.65 m walls 0.65 m. Still open: south-1, south-2-west, south-3 and north-east at 0.65 m. Later the same day: east of the house corner, south-2-west is replaced by the photographed 2.2 m patio wall with a door; west of it, in front of the house face, it stays 0.65 m (open).

The white wall with two doors along the west side of the junction lawns stood about 1.1-1.4 m too far west, with a 1.1 m jog the photos do not show, and both lawns stopped 0.4-0.5 m short of the lane kerb and well short of the wall, leaving a paved band the photos show as lawn. 17 November 2026: the wall refitted to the photographed foot (a straight run from Cervantes past the bed door, then the existing far length), the bed door and sill onto that run, the lawns and cross path to the measured kerbs and wall (0.10 m rms over 21 points, worst 0.19 m). Re-review 17 November 2026 (REVIEW.md): approved with limits; sixteen fresh reviewer picks fit at 0.15 m rms (straight run 0.09, far length 0.18 with a one-sided +0.17 m, i.e. the far length may stand about 0.15 m too far west). Still open: the far length's position, to be settled by a ground photo (request elena-south-cypress-wall-gate). The first fit was rejected in review (REVIEW.md) for picks on the wall face, an unsigned residual and the jog.

From the Elena 24 roof (ELENA-ROOF-2026-11-17.jpg) the far lawn ends at a white wall with two cypresses that runs from the west wall to the lane, and the lane passes its east end through a gate with a metal frame onto the middle pool lawn. The model ends the far lawn at the north face of registry 6265801UF1366N_part5, which stops at x = -148.5, and leaves open paving from there to the lane and the pool. At 22-40 m the roof camera cannot fix the wall's depth to better than about 1 m, and its photographed base runs nearly square to the view where the registry face is 30 degrees off it. Photo request elena-south-cypress-wall-gate asks for the ground views. 18 November 2026: built the white cypress wall (lane_walls.json elena-south-cypress-wall, 2.0 m) 0.35 m beyond the far lawn's edge, from the west wall to just short of the lane kerb, as an estimate (about 1 m in depth), and left generated porches and openings off the plain north face of registry 6265801UF1366N_part5 behind it (plain_fronts.json elena-south-far-blank-face). Existing photos checked: IMG_2261 and IMG_2330 show the wall face-on but their cameras are not solved; IMG_2683 and IMG_2684 look back from beside the far lawn but have the wall behind them; IMG_2681, IMG_2682 and IMG_2506 show the lane past the houses to the middle-pool gate, which is already modelled (middle_pool_north.json). The photo request stays open to fix the wall's line.

North end of the west wall: ELENA-ROOF-2026-11-17.jpg shows a tall white wall facing Cervantes with a brown door and the CALLE ELENA tile sign at its corner, enclosing the patio (parasol) west of the near lawn. The model has the 0.65 m cervantes-patio-south-2 there and no door (see also cervantes-kerb-walls-height). 17 November 2026: built as lane_walls.json cervantes-elena-patio-front-wall, 2.2 m with a 0.95 m brown door, from the house corner (registry part5 corner 32) to the CALLE ELENA corner on the Cervantes south line; the door placed through the solved roof camera (also IMG_2467, IMG_2264). The 0.65 m wall there is gone; the rest of cervantes-patio-south-2-west stays in front of the house face. The CALLE ELENA tile sign and the bougainvillea are detail, not drawn. Structure review, 18 November: lowered to 1.9 m (wall top cast at 1.84-1.95 m), with the door 1.8 m. The west wall's north end may be too tall as well (2.2 m); open. 18 November, later: the west wall's north end could not be measured, since its top is covered by bougainvillea and the planting along it in both roof photos. In IMG_2262 the CALLE ELENA plaques sit about 0.82 of the way up the face, which fits 2.1-2.2 m if they are at about 1.75 m. Left at 2.2 m.

Detail for after the structure review: the three lawn trees are generic trees where the photos show clipped domes and a clipped standard; the two cypresses against the far wall, the shrubs at the west wall foot, the bougainvillea on the walls and the lamp post are not drawn. The tree positions are estimates (their trunk bases are hidden in the roof views). 18 November 2026: built in Show details (data/elena_junction_details.json, src/elena-junction-details.ts): the lawn trees as clipped domes and a clipped standard re-placed through the roof cameras, the two cypresses at the far wall, bougainvillea on the west wall and over the corner patio wall, vines on the far part of the west wall and along the cypress wall, the lamp post in the east hedge bed and the CALLE ELENA tile plaques. Still not drawn: the shrubs in the strip at the west wall's foot, the bougainvillea on the foreground garden wall north of Cervantes beyond what was there, the corner house's white balcony ledge and porch surround, and the small window in the blank face behind the cypress wall. 18 November, later: added shrubs at the west wall's foot, the corner house's balcony ledge on two white piers (cast onto the registry face through IMG_2358; the photographed porch front is solid with an arched doorway, so the piers are approximate) and the small window on the blank face behind the cypress wall (cast through the roof camera).

East side of Elena south between Cervantes and the far wall: ELENA-ROOF-2026-11-17.jpg and IMG_2358 show planted beds with bougainvillea and a lamp post between the lane tiles and the front patio walls of the houses; the model has the lane against white walls with a grey margin and no beds. 18 November 2026: the clipped hedge beds between the lane and the corner house's patio wall and front are built (data/elena_south_beds.json, s 0.95-9.85 m), width from the solved roof camera; the hedge is planted against the back of each bed in 0.36 m pieces so it clears the shared route guard. South of 9.9 m the registry house fronts come within 0.15-0.4 m of the lane and nothing is built; the lamp post is detail. Structure review, 18 November: the beds now start at the photographed tile edge, 1.0 m east of the centreline. They are only 0.25-0.3 m deep up to the modelled patio wall and house face, where the photos show a hedge about 0.6-0.8 m deep: the corner patio wall (elena-south-mouth-patio-wall) is probably further east than drawn. Open. 18 November, later: checked whether the corner patio wall and house front stand further east, as a thicker hedge would need. The two solved roof cameras disagree: IMG_2358 casts the wall top behind the hedge at 1.7-2.0 m east of the centreline and the hedge face at 1.0 m, ELENA-ROOF-2026-11-17 at 1.4 m and 1.2-1.3 m. The modelled wall and registry face at 1.4 m lie between them, so nothing is moved; a ground photo square to the lane would settle it.

The near Elena lawn's north edge (the Cervantes south kerb, cervantes-patio-south-2) is inferred: both roof photos have it behind the foreground garden wall. Two readings say it is 0.6-0.8 m further north than modelled: the Elena south lane kerb is seen through the solved Elena 24 roof camera down to z = 58.44, where the model's lawn corner is at 59.07, and the clipped standard tree's trunk casts to z 59.0-59.4 through both roof cameras, at or beyond the modelled edge. Moving it would narrow or shift Cervantes at the junction (mapped 1.2 m wide, kerb lines 0.88 m either side of the centreline), which needs a ground camera solved at the junction (IMG_2262, IMG_2286 or IMG_2328 with the drain, the ramp kerb and the CALLE ELENA corner). The drain's position along Cervantes is not affected: the lane kerb runs square to Cervantes. 18 November, later: IMG_2286 shows the Cervantes cross-section at the drain square to the camera: about 2.0 m from the lawn kerb to the north bed wall, counted on the 0.4 m ramp tiles, against 1.73 m in the model. That argues for the lawn kerb a little further south, not 0.6-0.8 m north, so the roof readings (at the edge of what those cameras resolve) and the ground photo conflict; nothing is moved. The clipped standard keeps its cast position with its crown over the kerb.

The corner patio wall and the raised bed are built from the registry house line, the mapped lanes and tile counts; rough camera fits of IMG_2455, IMG_2800, IMG_2966 and IMG_2967 to the bed corner (structure review, 18 November 2026) agree with each other to about 0.2 m and put the corner 0.2-0.3 m from the model, within the stated 0.5 m. No solved camera sees it; photo request elena-north-corner-square asks for a view that could be solved.
The brown double door in the corner patio wall: no photo shows its sill or the patio floor level behind it, so the door stands on the lane ground with no step.

North of the raised corner bed, a lower kerbed bed runs along the house front under its barred windows on the west side of Elena north (IMG_2686, IMG_2969, with a trained climber on a wall with a stone shelf). It is not modelled; the two white planter boxes of elena_north.json stand in it.

Structure review of the Elena north corner (18 November 2026): in IMG_2800 and IMG_2799 the kerb corner of the hedged tree bed east of the mouth lines up with the corner bed's Cervantes face (about 0.9 m north of the Cervantes axis); the model has its south face about 0.6 m further north (1.5 m). Not moved: an existing feature outside this task, from rough fits only.

The Elena 24 garden-door wall on Cervantes is modelled 1.9 m high; IMG_2463 reads about 2.4-2.5 m beside the door, stepping up at a pier to 2.6-2.7 m where it meets the corner patio wall (structure review of the Elena north corner, 18 November 2026). Not changed here.

The magnolia with seed cones whose crown shows over the CALLE DE ELENA wall (IMG_2455, IMG_2965) stands in the hedged tree bed east of the Elena north mouth (bearing about 283 degrees from IMG_2455's fitted camera, against 289 for elena-north-tree-bed-2), above its lantana; its limbs reach west over the wall and it is most likely the dark canopy over the corner pocket on the aerial. The model has a pollarded tree there. A tree first placed inside the corner patio was removed in the detail review: the house's south gallery shows clear above the wall where it stood.
